findings.title: traceID field dropped from "grafana-data-egress" log events
findings.body: The previous implementation of LoggerMiddleware.logRequest appended a `traceID` field (obtained via `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)`) to the "Plugin Request Completed" log line. The new implementation logs only status, duration, eventName, time_before_plugin_request and error, plus whatever contextual attributes ContextualLoggerMiddleware injects — and `instrumentContext` (contextual_logger_middleware.go:27-37) only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname, not traceID. Unless `log.FromContext` automatically derives the trace ID from the span in the context, every "grafana-data-egress" log event loses its trace correlation, which breaks linking these egress log events to traces for anyone consuming them. This should either be verified against the infra log FromContext implementation or the traceID attribute should be added to instrumentContext.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new logger, discarding the receiver's recorded state
findings.body: `func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger { return NewTestLogger() }` returns a fresh instance and throws away `f`. LoggerMiddleware now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go:58), so any test that creates a TestLogger, runs the middleware, and asserts on `logger.InfoLogs.Calls` / `Message` / `Ctx` will see zero calls — the log records go to the throwaway instance. The fake should return `f` (and ideally replay the contextual attributes from the context) so tests can actually assert on the new contextual logging behavior; as written it makes the fake unusable for testing exactly the code path this PR introduces.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no tests, and LoggerMiddleware's log fields are now silently dependent on chain ordering
findings.body: The PR adds a brand-new middleware (ContextualLoggerMiddleware) with zero test coverage, and simultaneously changes LoggerMiddleware so that its "Plugin Request Completed" lines no longer read pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname from the request itself but rely on ContextualLoggerMiddleware appearing earlier in the middleware chain (pluginsintegration.go:159-161). Both constructors are exported, so LoggerMiddleware used standalone — or a future reordering of CreateMiddlewares — will silently emit log lines missing the plugin identity fields, with nothing failing. The old InstrumentationMiddleware even carried a doc comment saying it must live at the top of the stack; that constraint is now implicit and untested. A test asserting that LoggerMiddleware's output contains the contextual fields (and/or that the middleware pair is wired correctly) is needed.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported Logger interface is a breaking change for external implementers
findings.body: The `Logger` interface in the importable package pkg/plugins/log gains a required `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` method. Any out-of-tree implementation of this interface (e.g., in Grafana Enterprise or external code that constructs its own logger to pass into NewLoggerMiddleware / plugin services) will fail to compile after this change. Since the PR is described as a pure rename/refactor, the interface break should be called out, or a default provided, so downstream consumers can prepare.

findings.title: Rename is incomplete: test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware and logger still named "plugin.instrumentation"
findings.body: The PR's stated purpose is renaming instrumentation to metrics/logging, but the test function is still `TestInstrumentationMiddleware` (metrics_middleware_test.go:21), and the logger passed to NewLoggerMiddleware is still created as `log.New("plugin.instrumentation")` (pluginsintegration.go:161). Since these identifiers surface in test output and in actual log records (the logger name appears in every "Plugin Request Completed" line), the stale names are user-visible and should be updated for consistency with the rename.
